title: Toronto police officer facing new charge for role in teen's suicide at High Park
subtitle: Const. Kyle Upjohn has been charged with breach of trust, criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessities of life
article: A Toronto police officer is facing a new charge for his role in the suicide of a 19-year-old man after an investigation by Ontario's police watchdog in June previously resulted in two other charges being laid.

Const. Kyle Upjohn was charged with breach of trust on Thursday. Upjohn had previously been charged with criminal negligence causing death and failing to provide the necessities of life for a 2016 incident at High Park. A charge of criminal negligence causing death comes with a maximum sentence of life in prison.
According to the SIU, a man sought the help of a police officer in relation to a suicide attempt on February 2, 2016. Less than two hours later, the suicidal teen was pronounced dead at the scene.

Upjohn allegedly refused to help a man who was warning him about the teen's suicide attempt because he was on another call, according to City News . Upjohn allegedly told the man, whose wife saw the teen hang a rope, to call 911 instead.
Upjohn has been suspended with pay. According to the Ontario Sunshine List, he earned $106,000 in 2015.
He made his first court appearance on Thursday at Old City Hall to answer to the charges.
